plan:
COMPLETE EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN — "GPT-2 vs CodeLlama-7b-Python on RepoBench Python cross_file_first (next-line auto-completion)"

Status: DESIGN ONLY. No experiment was run. Any number below is a plan assumption or predicted budget, never a measured result.

════════════════════════════════════════════
0. RESEARCH QUESTION → TESTABLE FORM
════════════════════════════════════════════
RQ: How does a small general-text LM (GPT-2 family) compare with a large code-specialized LM (CodeLlama-7b-Python) on repository-level NEXT-LINE completion in the cross_file_first setting of RepoBench Python?

Testable decomposition (all zero-shot):
- Q1 (capability at equal context): mean Exact Match and mean Edit Similarity difference when both models receive ≤1,000 tokens of cross-file context (matched condition). Primary estimand: ΔEM = EM(CodeLlama-7b-Python) − EM(GPT-2-<size>) and ΔES analog.
- Q2 (system-level with native windows): same comparison when each model uses its own max context (GPT-2 ≤1,024; CodeLlama ≤16,384 minus completion budget). This is the "deployed-system" comparison.
- Q3 (sensitivity): does the ordering or conclusion change between matched and native? Reported explicitly as an interaction, never collapsed into one number (Research suggestion #3).
- Q4 (exploratory, secondary): pass@k on a subsample; token-overlap and chrF partial-credit; effect of retrieval-order permutation (baseline).

════════════════════════════════════════════
1. FIXED TASK REQUIREMENTS vs ASSUMPTIONS
════════════════════════════════════════════
FIXED (task-defining, not negotiable):
- Dataset: official released RepoBench Python benchmark, setting = cross_file_first (RCF), i.e., completion must be predicted from cross-file context (other files of the same repo) with NO same-file/previous-line context. Use the retrieval context SHIPPED with the dataset (standard BM25, provided top-K files); no re-retrieval — retrieval is not a variable.
- Official splits: use the official test split as released; report train/valid only if a fine-tuning condition is ever added (it is NOT in this design).
- Official metrics: Exact Match (EM) and Edit Similarity (ES) computed with the released official evaluation script. EM and ES are CO-PRIMARY here (Rationale: single-line EM in code completion is typically very low, so ES/partial-credit carries most signal — Research suggestion #1; both are official so no extra burden).
- The question's mention of pass@k is honored ONLY as a clearly-labeled, secondary, non-official addition.

ASSUMPTIONS (stated, testable at execution):
- A1 Dataset provenance: canonical copy = official RepoBench repo / its HuggingFace artifact for Python; test ≈4,000 instances (approximate count to verify at download).
- A2 Models = HuggingFace checkpoints: gpt2, gpt2-medium, gpt2-large, gpt2-xl; codellama/CodeLlama-7b-Python-hf. If budget forces a single "small" model, default gpt2-large (774M).
- A3 Zero-shot inference; NO fine-tuning (keeps pipeline clean; fine-tuning is a separate study).
- A4 Budget: one 40 GB-class GPU-machine run (full test set greedy; subsample for sampling/pass@k). CPU-only is a documented fallback only.
- A5 "Performance" = next-line completion quality, primarily EM & ES; secondary metrics labeled non-official.
- A6 Execution environment is NOT this workspace (here: no network, no GPU, no ML libs, no data/weights — verified). Design executes on a provisioned networked+GPU box.

════════════════════════════════════════════
2. EXPERIMENTAL UNITS, FACTORS, CONDITIONS
════════════════════════════════════════════
Units: the official test instances (i = 1..N, N≈4,000). Paired design — every model/condition sees the SAME instances in the SAME order.

Factor A — Model (5 levels): gpt2, gpt2-medium, gpt2-large, gpt2-xl, CodeLlama-7b-Python. (GPT-2 family = size sweep so "small model" is a curve, not one arbitrary point.)
Factor B — Context policy (2 levels per model):
   • matched: truncate prompt to first 1,000 tokens for ALL models (≤ GPT-2 window; equalizes information actually feedable).
   • native: use each model's own window (GPT-2: 1,024−budget; CodeLlama: up to 16,384−budget). For GPT-2, matched and native are nearly identical (1,000 vs ~924 usable); the meaningful matched-vs-native difference is on CodeLlama.
Factor C — Decoding (2 modes): greedy (primary, deterministic) and sampling (secondary).
Baseline/control conditions: empty prediction; frequency baseline; retrieval-order permutations (random, reverse) on a subset and for at least CodeLlama-native + gpt2-large-matched to quantify sensitivity to the provided ordering.

Cross-product: greedy run = 5 models × 2 context policies (10 pipelines) over N instances. Sampling/pass@k = subsample S≈400–500 stratified instances × n=5 samples × {gpt2-large, gpt2-xl, CodeLlama} × both policies (bounded budget).

════════════════════════════════════════════
3. DATA PIPELINE & PROMPT CONSTRUCTION
════════════════════════════════════════════
P0 Download & hash: record dataset commit/version, HF artifact hash, transformers/torch versions; freeze them in the report.
P1 Prompt builder: replicate EXACTLY the official RCF template from the official retrieval_based_autocomplete.py — concatenate retrieved files each prefixed by a "# Path: {path}" header, followed by the official sentinel line naming the target file (e.g., "# The code you need to complete is located in the file: {target}"). Reconstruct from the official source at implementation time; do NOT re-derive from memory (template exactness is a required sanity check, §6).
P2 Tokenization per model (each model's own tokenizer — this is part of the model system; no cross-model tokenizer sharing).
P3 Truncation: matched → keep first 1,000 tokens; native → keep first (max window − completion_budget) with completion_budget = 100 tokens. Truncate from the END, preserving earliest (repository-overview) context, consistent with official behavior.
P4 Record per instance: prompt_length_tokens, truncated_flag, num_retrieved_files_actually_used, retrieved_token_count, and whether the gold completion line (or its distinctive tokens) appears in the retained context (context-quality proxy). These feed stratified analysis and truncation reporting.

════════════════════════════════════════════
4. INFERENCE & DECODING
════════════════════════════════════════════
- Greedy: max_new_tokens = 100; extract the FIRST COMPLETE LINE of the generation as the prediction (official comparison is line-level). Record raw generation too.
- Sampling (pass@k): top-p = 0.8, temperature = 0.8, n = 5 samples/instance, fixed distinct global seeds (logged). Same line-extraction.
- Precision: CodeLlama fp16/bf16; GPT-2 fp32 or bf16. Batch size tuned to VRAM (CodeLlama bsz 4–8 at matched; smaller at 16k native).
- Log per instance: wall time, tokens/sec, VRAM peak, generated tokens, truncated/empty flags.

════════════════════════════════════════════
5. METRICS & EVALUATION (official eval script)
════════════════════════════════════════════
Primary (official):
- EM[i] = 1{extracted_line == gold_line}; report mean EM and per-instance vector.
- ES[i] = official edit similarity (1 − normalized Levenshtein) between extracted line and gold line; report mean ES and per-instance vector. ES is CO-PRIMARY, computed by the same official script for both models.
Secondary (all labeled NON-official):
- token-window overlap: |pred_tokens ∩ gold_tokens| / |gold_tokens| (and Jaccard) for partial credit.
- chrF (character n-gram F-score) for character-level partial credit (Research suggestion #1).
- pass@k: line-level exact match over n=5 samples (pass@1..5, ES@5 = best ES over samples) on the subsample.
- Diagnostic rates: empty-prediction rate, truncated-completion rate, mean/median prediction length, per-repo means.
All metrics computed by the SAME script for both models (no per-model eval variants).

════════════════════════════════════════════
6. SANITY CHECKS BEFORE FULL RUN (viability)
════════════════════════════════════════════
(S1) Template fidelity unit test: for 3 hand-crafted instances, assert the builder output byte-matches the official script output (golden-file diff). Fail ⇒ stop.
(S2) Smoke test: 10–20 instances × every model×condition; verify no crashes, VRAM fits, output lengths sane, empty-rate not pathological, gold line is achievable (manual review of ≥5 outputs per model).
(S3) Performance probe: measure tokens/sec and s/instance on the smoke batch; EXTRAPOLATE to N≈4k and validate the budget in §9 with ≥2× margin; adjust batch size if needed.
(S4) Determinism: rerun greedy on the smoke set twice; assert identical outputs (same hardware/seed) before trusting paired comparisons.
(S5) Baseline sanity: empty/frequency baselines computed — EM of baselines should be ~0 and ES small but >0; if a model matches baseline EM it is flagged as non-informative.
(S6) Truncation audit: verify matched condition truly yields ≤1,000 tokens for 100% of instances and report native truncation rates (how often CodeLlama's 16k window is exhausted).

════════════════════════════════════════════
7. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS PLAN (pre-specified)
════════════════════════════════════════════
- Estimates: mean EM, mean ES, and differences ΔEM, ΔES for (a) matched and (b) native, for every GPT-2 size vs CodeLlama. Report all four model sizes (never only one) to show the small-model size trend.
- Uncertainty: 95% paired bootstrap CIs over the instance index (10,000 resamples). Paired tests: McNemar on per-instance EM; paired difference test / permutation on ES. Report Cohen's h effect size for EM.
- Stratified (mechanism): split instances by (i) retrieved-context length (low/mid/high cross-file need), (ii) context-quality proxy (gold tokens present in context or not), (iii) repo size. Report ΔEM/ΔES within strata to test whether any CodeLlama advantage concentrates in high-context-need slices.
- Matched-vs-native reporting protocol (Research suggestion #3): report THREE headline numbers, never one: (1) Δ(EM, ES) matched; (2) Δ(EM, ES) native; (3) the within-model change Δnative−matched for CodeLlama (the "context-window dividend" attributable to 16k window). State the conclusion under each condition and explicitly state whether the model ordering is stable; if they differ, the report must say the conclusion is condition-dependent rather than pick one.
- Sensitivity bounds: recompute ΔEM for the retrieval-order permutations (random/reverse) to bound how much the provided ordering alone explains any gap.
- Sample retention: log any dropped instances (empty gold, decode failure, OOM) and re-run the paired analysis on the intersection.

════════════════════════════════════════════
8. COMPUTE/BUDGET & FEASIBILITY
════════════════════════════════════════════
- This workspace CANNOT run it (verified: no network, no GPU, no torch/transformers/datasets, no data/weights). Execution requires a provisioned box.
- Target hardware: 1× A100/H100 40 GB (CodeLlama fp16 ≈14–16 GB VRAM; bsz 4–8). GPT-2 needs ≤3 GB.
- Predicted budget (to be validated by S3, not measured yet): full-test greedy ≈ 2–5 GPU-hours (CodeLlama dominated; native-16k prompts dominate; GPT-2 negligible). Sampling/pass@k subsample 500×5 adds ≈1–3 GPU-hours. Total ≈ 0.5–1.5 A100-days.
- Software: pip install torch transformers datasets accelerate evaluate huggingface_hub; git clone official RepoBench for scripts/eval; pins recorded.
- Reduced-budget fallback (documented, lower fidelity): stratified n=500, gpt2-large only, matched-greedy only, CodeLlama 4-bit CPU (llama.cpp) only if no GPU — flagged as non-headline.

════════════════════════════════════════════
9. REPORTING / DELIVERABLES
════════════════════════════════════════════
- Main table: per model×condition: mean EM, mean ES, secondary metrics, empty/truncated rates, mean context tokens.
- Difference table: ΔEM/ΔES with 95% CI and p-value (matched and native rows) for each GPT-2 size vs CodeLlama; the matched-vs-native interaction row.
- Figures: ES distribution (box/violin) per model; EM by strata; ΔEM vs GPT-2 parameter count (size trend).
- Transparent artifacts: seed list, dataset/model/library versions + hashes, full config JSON, per-instance result CSV, reproduction script.
- Explicit statement in conclusion: no claim of measured results from this design; all numbers are to be generated at execution time.

════════════════════════════════════════════
10. LIMITATIONS & UNCERTAINTIES
════════════════════════════════════════════
- Inherent confound: size + code-specialization + model family co-vary; controls (equal context, greedy, same eval/instances) remove the context-window and decoding explanations but attribution to "scale" vs "specialization" vs "family" is NOT identifiable from this design — the conclusion is about MODEL SYSTEMS (small general vs large code-specialized), wording chosen accordingly.
- Exact official template/instance JSON layout reconstructed from official source at implementation (not from memory; S1 guards it).
- Dataset canonical artifact/size approximate (~4k test) until download.
- pass@k/chrF/token-overlap are non-official additions (labeled).
- Single-line EM may be near-floor; this is why ES is co-primary and partial-credit metrics are included (Research suggestion #1).
- Budget numbers are predictions to be validated by the S3 probe, not measurements.
